chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Samāʿah, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام), who said:

Indeed, in the Book of ʿAlī (عليه السلام) it is stated that the most severely afflicted of people are the Prophets, then the successors, then the most exemplary and then the next most exemplary. The believer is afflicted only in accordance with the measure of his good deeds. So whoever has sound religion and good deeds, his affliction becomes more intense. That is because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, did not make the world a reward for a believer nor a punishment for a disbeliever. And whoever has a feeble religion and weak deeds, his affliction is less. And affliction is swifter to the God-conscious believer than rain is to the low ground of the earth.

key_terms.أَعْمَالِهِ الْحَسَنَةِ: his good deeds, which are a measure of the believer’s trials
key_terms.الدُّنْيَا: the worldly life, which is not the final reward or punishment
key_terms.النَّبِيُّونَ: the Prophets, who endure the greatest tests
key_terms.الْمُؤْمِنُ: the believer whose trials correspond to his spiritual state
key_terms.الْوَصِيُّونَ: the successors appointed after the Prophets
key_terms.بَلَاءً: trial, affliction, or tribulation sent upon a person
key_terms.دِينُهُ: his religion, meaning the soundness and firmness of his faith

ai.seo_question: Why do the Prophets and righteous believers face the most severe trials?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that the intensity of tribulation is not a sign of divine rejection; rather, the Prophets and their successors face the greatest trials, followed by the most virtuous believers. It explains that worldly ease is not the true reward of the believer, and worldly hardship often corresponds to spiritual rank and righteous deeds.
